title: Zoom in: the ingest API's admission decision when space runs out
caption: Every answer is local and takes microseconds: the gateway's quota, the data's class, and room in that class's buffer. Billing reads wait; diagnostics are dropped.

steps.text: A batch arrives from an edge gateway, tagged with its class and the gateway's id.
The gateway is within its share of the admit rate (a token bucket per gateway).
It is a billing read: must-keep, so it may wait but never be dropped.
The log is under its bound (measured in minutes of validator work, not in bytes).
Append to the replicated log, then acknowledge. Only the ack lets the gateway delete its copy.

scenarios.name: Log full: billing read
scenarios.summary: A must-keep read is never dropped; it is refused politely and stays on the gateway's disk.

steps.text: Same checks: in quota, billing class.
Validators are behind and the log is at its bound.
429 with Retry-After: 60 plus jitter. The gateway keeps the batch and retries; the API spent microseconds on it.

scenarios.name: Queue full: diagnostics
scenarios.summary: Sheddable data is accepted and dropped on our side, so the gateway does not retry it.

steps.text: A voltage sample arrives from a gateway within its quota.
Drop the oldest sample in the queue to make room and answer 202. A fresh voltage reading is worth more than a stale one, and the drop is counted in metrics.

scenarios.name: Tower reconnects
scenarios.summary: A tower that was down for 6 hours replays its backlog at line speed. The per-gateway quota keeps one flood from starving every other gateway.

steps.text: 20 000 meters behind one tower buffered 6 hours of quarter-hour data: ~500 000 messages arrive at once.
The gateway's quota is 500 batches/s. The excess gets 429 and stays on its disk, so the replay takes ~16 minutes instead of seconds.
What is admitted follows the normal path: billing reads into the log, diagnostics older than an hour dropped as expired. Other gateways never notice.
